body: New York Supreme Court Justice Francis Kahn on November 11, 2026 denied summary judgment to 109Co in its $44 million foreclosure against Fortuna Realty's Hotel Hayden, finding that the note and mortgage had not been properly attached to each other, The Real Deal reported. The ruling sends the case to trial.

The 122-room hotel is at 127 West 28th Street in Manhattan. Fortuna bought it in 1999 and refinanced it with Morgan Stanley Private Bank in 2018. Morgan Stanley started the foreclosure in April 2025 and, in February 2026, sold the loan for an undisclosed price to 109Co, a firm formed in 2023. Default is not in dispute: according to the report, the owner's principal signed a forbearance agreement admitting it.

The dispute is over standing. A foreclosing lender has to show how and when it came to hold the note along with the mortgage, and courts have required the papers to be "so firmly affixed thereto as to become a part thereof." The Real Deal reported that Morgan Stanley filed the note and mortgage separately when it refinanced the hotel, and Justice Kahn found the requirement was not met. The rule protects borrowers from a second party later claiming the same debt and trying to foreclose again. These challenges became common in the foreclosures after the 2007 housing crash, and they usually come up after a loan has changed hands.

"No staple, no case," the borrower's attorney told The Real Deal. He said 109Co must now try to prove its standing at trial or go back and fix the attachment problem, which could be hard if it means finding people involved in the 2018 loan, and that he expects more such challenges as banks sell off bad loans. Representatives of 109Co and Fortuna could not immediately be reached. The ruling gives the hotel owner more leverage in any settlement talks.

timeline.label: Fortuna Realty buys the Hotel Hayden
Morgan Stanley Private Bank refinances the hotel
Morgan Stanley sells the loan to 109Co
Justice Kahn denies summary judgment over note attachment; case headed to trial
